data.title: Run a toy gripper contact experiment
data.summary: A generic two-finger gripper, one box and three friction trials. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: MuJoCo simulates articulated structures interacting through contact.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender / MuJoCo environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: A generic two-finger gripper, one box and three friction trials.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent gripper contact workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: A generic two-finger gripper, one box and three friction trials. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Reuse a documented MuJoCo model and name the contact bodies explicitly
Run a bounded close-and-lift sequence with fixed initial conditions
Log contact forces, object slip and lift height before visualizing the replay

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.

validation: The recorded object height agrees with the replayed trajectory
Failed grasps remain in the results instead of being removed
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: Simulation cannot authorize operation of a physical robot or certify a safe grasp.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.

tips: Inspect solver warnings and time-step sensitivity before interpreting force values.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me run a toy gripper contact experiment in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: A generic two-finger gripper, one box and three friction trials. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: The recorded object height agrees with the replayed trajectory; Failed grasps remain in the results instead of being removed. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
